text:
ariane: Quick sync — we need a single checklist for how timeouts/cancels should behave across SDKs (Node/Python/Go/Rust/mobile) and what gets propagated to the server. TL;DR: users keep getting strange retries or orphaned streams. Can we align? :thinking:
jordan: I can draft. Main confusion: per-request AbortController vs client-level timeout. In Node we default to attaching a per-request AbortController when user doesn't provide one, which cancels local stream handlers but our retry layer sometimes spawns a fresh request and the previous socket lingers server-side.
sam: +1. In Python (asyncio + httpx) we use httpx.Timeout which raises a TimeoutException — coroutine cancelled — but unless we explicitly close the response/connection the server may still be streaming. We need a pattern to always close the underlying transport on cancel.
lee: Go's context cancellation is pretty explicit: cancel the request's Context -> net/http cancels the transport and we get connection close that should propagate. However gRPC and HTTP/2 need an explicit RST or grpc.Cancel to ensure server stops work quickly.
pranav: Is the expected behavior: "client cancel => best-effort server cancel" or must we guarantee server sees cancel immediately? We need a spec: best-effort is fine for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private we should attempt strong propagation.
ariane: Proposal: 1) Per-request timeout/cancel should cancel streaming handlers AND close transport. 2) If cancel happens mid-stream, SDK should send an explicit stream termination (RST or HTTP/2 FIN) when possible. 3) Retries should not be attempted if a user-initiated cancel/AbortController triggered. 4) Client-level timeouts (SDK config) behave like an operator-level policy and can trigger retries/fallbacks.
jordan: Implementation notes for Node: use AbortController for both fetch and our internal stream manager. When user passes AbortSignal, treat it as authoritative -> no retries. When we synthesize a timeout AbortSignal, mark it as retryable and run retry policy. Example snippet we discussed earlier:
```js
// userAbort optional, sdkTimeoutMs optional
const controller = new AbortController();
const mergedSignal = mergeSignals(userAbort, controller.signal);
const resp = await fetch(url, { signal: mergedSignal });
// on sdk-timeout: controller.abort(); // mark as retryable
// on userAbort: userAbort already aborted -> no retry
```
sam: For Python, pattern is similar: accept user-provided "cancel_token" or "Timeout". If user provides cancel -> raise and do not retry. If SDK enforces timeout, close response explicitly and allow retry. Pseudo:
```py
with httpx.AsyncClient() as c:
    try:
        resp = await c.stream("GET", url, timeout=our_timeout)
    except httpx.ReadTimeout:
        await resp.aclose()  # ensure transport closed
        raise RetryableError
    except UserCancelledError:
        await resp.aclose()
        raise
```
lee: For Go, ensure we call `req.Context()` cancellation and then `transport.CancelRequest(req)` (for older clients) or close the underlying body. For gRPC, call `grpc.ClientConn.Close()` or use grpc context cancellation so server interceptor sees it immediately.
pranav: Tests we need: 1) e2e stream where server logs on-cancel and we assert server saw cancel within 1s of client cancel. 2) Retry suppression test: user Abort => no retry; SDK timeout => retry. 3) Resource leak test: open 200 concurrent streams, cancel half, ensure no lingering goroutines/sockets beyond threshold.
jordan: I put a WIP PR for Node streaming teardown: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/223. It changes our retry wrapper to check `signal.aborted` before starting a retry and sends a FIN on fetch by calling `resp.body.cancel()` where available. Needs review. :eyes:
pranav: I added a Python PR with the explicit `resp.aclose()` on our timeout branch: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/88. CI failing on flake related to test timing.
ci-bot: PR #223: tests 12/14 passing, flake in stream-cancel test. PR #88: tests 37/40 passing, one flaky integration timeout.
ariane: Action items: Jordan & Pranav coordinate a common test harness (simple server that streams and records cancel events). Sam & Lee add language-specific teardown snippets to the SDK docs. I'll consolidate checklist into the SDK deprecation/migration doc and call for a cross-team review. Can we aim to ship aligned behavior in next 2 sprints?
jordan: I'll pair with Sam tomorrow to prototype the harness. reallocating time now. :thumbsup:
sam: I'll add a test that asserts server RST/connection close seen in logs, and mark it flaky-safe with retries in CI.
lee: I'll audit Go/gRPC paths for explicit Cancel propagation and open a small PR if I find places where we rely on GC to close things.
pranav: Ping me when you want the CLA/enterprise test infra added.
ariane: Thanks all. If anyone hits an immediate production issue (or sees orphaned GPU work), post in #incidents and tag me. Closing the thread for now. :white_check_mark:
